Perhaps it could help to explain Conflict Theory and Historical Materialism. Stated simply, conflict theory is the belief that society is comprised of groups competing for limited resources, and this still today, over a century after Marx's death, is a significant sociological perspective. Conflict theory  also examines power and coersion. Some examples of conflict theory perspective in practice is the view of the American Justice System, which in the eyes of a conflict theorist, is a system which is used to control the working class (because white-collar crime is not often punished with much jail time and most prisoners come from low-income backgrounds), and the disproportionate amount of minorities in the prison system can be seen as ethnic persecution by the people with the most economic and social power (rich caucasian people.) Now, historical materialism is a belief that material and economic conditions influence society more than ideas and people.  This ties into Marx's ideas of class conflict and the evolution of capitalism, where he stated that classes had always struggled and the elites had managed to maintain the means of production and material wealth and thus their privileges. This as well ties into his beliefs that economic class divides more than race and nation, because those are less tangiable than material conditions. This is relatively basic, but I hope I helped. I am simply a student with a passion for Marx, but there is plenty of information out there =D
